subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without API keys

question: Should OpenClaw support keyless access to OpenCode Zen free models despite the current upstream Zen documentation requiring users to obtain and configure an API key?
rationale: The patch is technically targeted, but accepting an undocumented external auth mode determines the supported provider contract and cannot be resolved safely from a transient successful request alone.

options.title: Retain documented API-key auth
options.body: Remove the synthetic no-auth route and keep the existing OpenCode key requirement until the provider publishes a supported keyless API contract.

options.title: Adopt keyless Zen access
options.body: Land only after OpenCode documents or confirms the no-auth contract, its eligible model metadata, and the intended behavior when a free model is retired or becomes paid.

recommendation.title: Retain documented API-key auth
recommendation.body: Remove the synthetic no-auth route and keep the existing OpenCode key requirement until the provider publishes a supported keyless API contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Mainline history attribution for the OpenCode plugin and shared model-auth surface could not be established from the available read-only evidence.
